title: Create, update, or delete a rule set within an ad account
content_data:
Use this endpoint to create, update, or delete a rule set within an ad account. > **Note**
> - Creating rule sets is currently an allowlist-only feature. If you would like to access it, please contact your TikTok representative. > - You can create up to 20 rule sets for each ad account. ## Request **Endpoint** https://business-api.tiktok.com/open_api/v1.3/smart_plus/value_rule_set/create_or_update/ **Method** POST **Header** ```xtable |Field{35%}|Type{15%}|Description{50%}| |---|---|---| |Access-Token {Required}|string|Authorized access token. For details, see [Authentication](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs/marketing-api-authentication/v1.3).| |Content-Type {Required}|string|Request message type.
Allowed value: `application/json`.| ``` **Parameters** ```xtable |Field{35%}|Type{15%}|Description{50%}| |---|---|---| |advertiser_id {Required}|string|Advertiser ID.| |operation_type {Required}|string|Operation type.

Enum values:
  • `CREATE`: To create a new rule set.
  • `UPDATE`: To update an existing rule set.
  • `DELETE`: To delete an existing rule set.
| |value_rule_set {Required}|object|Details of the rule set.| #|value_rule_set_id {+Conditional}|string|
  • Required when `operation_type` is `UPDATE` or `DELETE`.
  • Not supported when `operation_type` is `CREATE`.

The ID of the rule set that you want to update or delete.

To retrieve existing rule sets within an ad account, use [/smart_plus/value_rule_set/get/](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs/get-rule-sets-within-an-ad-account/v1.3).| #|rule_set_name {+Conditional}|string|
  • Required when `operation_type` is `CREATE`.
  • Optional when `operation_type` is `UPDATE`.
  • Not supported when `operation_type` is `DELETE`.

The name of the rule set.

Length limit: 512 characters.

Note: Duplicate rule set names are not supported.| #|rules {+Conditional}|object[]|

  • Required when `operation_type` is `CREATE`.
  • Optional when `operation_type` is `UPDATE`.
  • Not supported when `operation_type` is `DELETE`.

Details of rules in the rule set.

Each rule set can contain up to 10 rules.

Note: Duplicate rules or criteria are not supported in one rule set.| ##|order {+Conditional}|number|Required when `rules` is specified.

The order of the rule in the rule set.

Use consecutive integers starting from 1 (for example, 1, 2, and 3, rather than 1, 3, and 5).

When you configure multiple rules in a rule set, this order indicates their priority. The system will prioritize rule application based on the rule order. If a person meets the criteria for multiple rules, we'll only apply the first applicable rule in the list.
For example:
Rule 1: Increase bid by 20% for ages 25–34 in the United States
Rule 2: Increase bid by 50% for iOS operating system
So a US-based iOS user aged 25–34 matches both rules, but only gets a 20% bid increase because Rule 1 comes first.| ##|rule_id|string|Valid only when `operation_type` is `UPDATE`.

Rule ID.

  • When this field is specified, the `rule_id` will stay the same after the rule set update.
  • When this field is not specified, the system will generate a new `rule_id` after the rule set update.
| ##|rule_name {+Conditional}|string|Required when `rules` is specified.

Rule name.| ##|criteria {+Conditional}|object[]|Required when `rules` is specified.

Details of criteria for the rule.

You can specify up to two criteria per rule. If you include two criteria in a single rule, the system triggers the rule only when a person meets both criteria.| ###|criteria_type {+Conditional}|string|Required when `criteria` is specified.

Criterion type.

Enum values:
  • `CRITERIA_TYPE_GENDER`: Genders.
  • `CRITERIA_TYPE_AGE`: Ages.
  • `CRITERIA_TYPE_LOCATION`: Locations.
  • `CRITERIA_TYPE_OS`: Operating systems.
  • `CRITERIA_TYPE_AUDIENCE`: Audience
| ###|value {+Conditional}|object|Required when `criteria` is specified.

Details of value or values for the criterion.| ####|gender {+Conditional}|string|Required when `criteria_type` is `CRITERIA_TYPE_GENDER`.

Gender.

Enum values:
  • `GENDER_MALE`: Male.
  • `GENDER_FEMALE`: Female.
| ####|age_groups {+Conditional}|string[]|Required when `criteria_type` is `CRITERIA_TYPE_AGE`.

A list of age groups.

Enum values:
  • `AGE_18_24`: 18-24.
  • `AGE_25_34`: 25-34.
  • `AGE_35_44`: 35-44.
  • `AGE_45_54`: 45-54.
  • `AGE_55_100`: 55+.
| ####|location {+Conditional}|object|Required when `criteria_type` is `CRITERIA_TYPE_LOCATION`.

Details of values for the location criterion.| #####|location_ids {+Conditional}|string[]|Required when `location` is specified.

A list of location IDs.
  • To get the available locations and corresponding IDs based on your placement and objective, use the [/tool/targeting/search/](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs/search-for-location-targeting-tags/v1.3) or [/tool/region/](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs/get-available-locations-by-different-settings/v1.3) endpoint.
  • To get the list of location IDs, see [Location IDs](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs/location-ids/v1.3).
| ####|operating_systems {+Conditional}|string[]|Required when `criteria_type` is `CRITERIA_TYPE_OS`.

A list of operating systems.

Enum values:
  • `ANDROID`: Android.
  • `IOS`: iOS.
| ####|audience_ids {+Conditional}|string[]|Required when `criteria_type` is `CRITERIA_TYPE_AUDIENCE`.

A list of audience IDs.

The audience can be a custom audience, lookalike audience, or saved audience.

Max size: 5.

Ensure each audience is valid.
  • To retrieve valid custom or lookalike audience IDs within an ad account, use [/dmp/custom_audience/list/](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs/get-all-audiences/v1.3) and select audiences with `is_valid` as `true`.
  • To retrieve saved audience IDs within an ad account, use [/dmp/saved_audience/list/](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs/get-details-of-saved-audiences/v1.3).

Note: Duplicate audience IDs are not supported.| ##|adjust_percentage {+Conditional}|number|Required when `rules` is specified.

Bid adjustment percentage.

  • For bid increases: [1, 50].
  • For bid decreases: [-70, -1].

An `adjust_percentage` of -70 represents a bid decrease of 70% when the conditions defined in `criteria` are met.| ``` ### Example #### Create a rule set ```xcodeblock (code curl http) curl --location --request POST 'https://business-api.tiktok.com/open_api/v1.3/smart_plus/value_rule_set/create_or_update/' \ --header 'Access-Token: {{Access-Token}}' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ ---data '{ "advertiser_id": "{{advertiser_id}}", "operation_type": "CREATE", "value_rule_set": { "rule_set_name": "{{rule_set_name}}", "rules": [ { "order": 1, "rule_name": "{{rule_name}}", "criteria": [ { "criteria_type": "CRITERIA_TYPE_GENDER", "value": { "gender": "GENDER_FEMALE" } } ], "adjust_percentage": 10 } ] } }' (/code) ``` #### Update a rule set ```xcodeblock (code curl http) curl --location --request POST 'https://business-api.tiktok.com/open_api/v1.3/smart_plus/value_rule_set/create_or_update/' \ --header 'Access-Token: {{Access-Token}}' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{ "advertiser_id": "{{advertiser_id}}", "operation_type": "UPDATE", "value_rule_set": { "value_rule_set_id": "{{value_rule_set_id}}", "rule_set_name": "{{rule_set_name}}", "rules": [ { "order": 1, "rule_name": "{{rule_name}}", "criteria": [ { "criteria_type": "CRITERIA_TYPE_AUDIENCE", "value": { "audience_ids": [ "{{audience_ids}}" ] } } ], "adjust_percentage": 8 } ] } }' (/code) ``` #### Delete a rule set ```xcodeblock (code curl http) curl --location --request POST 'https://business-api.tiktok.com/open_api/v1.3/smart_plus/value_rule_set/create_or_update/' \ --header 'Access-Token: {{Access-Token}}' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{ "advertiser_id": "{{advertiser_id}}", "operation_type": "DELETE", "value_rule_set": { "value_rule_set_id": "{{value_rule_set_id}}" } }' (/code) ``` ## Response ```xtable |Field{30%}|Data Type{15%}|Description{55%}| |-|-|-| |code |number|Response code. For the complete list of response codes and descriptions, see [Appendix - Return Codes](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs/return-codes-appendix/v1.3).| |message |string|Response message. For details, see [Appendix - Return Codes](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs/return-codes-appendix/v1.3).| |request_id|string| The log ID of the request, which uniquely identifies a request.| |data|object|Returned data.| #|value_rule_set_id|string|The ID of the rule set.| ``` ### Example ```xcodeblock (code curl http) { "code": 0, "message": "OK", "request_id": "{{request_id}}", "data": { "value_rule_set_id": "{{value_rule_set_id}}" } } (/code) ```
